title: Drain the 47 `bad-citation` rows on `SHARED_RESOLVER_RESIDUAL` — a closed ledger with no owner is how it turns back into an allow-list
body:
Filed by the `domain:devx` execution PM seat (#6023) as the named owner for the residual PR #18100 (card #16898) deliberately left behind. ⚠️ `priority:` and `domain:` unset — triage's call.

## What PR #18100 left, and why leaving it was right

Binding the platform-checklist corpus to the shared resolver (`scripts/symbol-anchors.mjs`) withdrew a permissive token match. **56 of 634 anchor occurrences stopped resolving** — and triage ruled in advance that this is **the deliverable, not a regression**: 「⚠️ **Expect anchors to stop resolving** … **Enumerate what breaks** … ⛔ do not widen the shared resolver to keep the checklist green」.

Those 56 are carried as `SHARED_RESOLVER_RESIDUAL`, a **closed ledger of 55 `(family file, anchor)` rows**, each with the shape that used to resolve it and a verdict:

| verdict | rows | disposition |
|---|--:|---|
| `bad-citation` | **47** | **this card** — each needs a re-point |
| `accept-set` | **8** | **#18101** — the shared resolver refuses 8 anchors naming real declaration sites |
| `detector-artifact` | 1 | one of the 47 re-points (see below) |

## ⭐ Why this needs an owner rather than opportunistic drainage

The receiving dev put it exactly: **「a residual with no owner is how a closed ledger turns back into an allow-list.」**

The ledger is currently **exact in both directions**, and PR #18100 proved each edge by ablation:
- a row that stops firing ⇒ **STALE RESIDUAL ROW** red;
- an unlisted failure ⇒ ordinary **ABSENT SYMBOL** red;
- `SHARED_RESOLVER_RESIDUAL_CEILING = 55` ⇒ a 56th row is **refused**. Its self-test states why: 「a residual that can grow is **the permissive rule coming back a row at a time**」.

⇒ Rows can only leave **by repair**. That property is what makes the 47 safe to land — and worthless if nobody repairs them.

## ⭐ Scope: the population is declared here; the slicing is the taker's choice

The 47 rows sit across **12 area files** under `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/`, already grouped by family file in the ledger, each row carrying the shape that used to resolve it.

⚠️ **This is deliberately ONE card, not twelve.** The receiving dev recommended one card per area file; this seat rules otherwise, and says why: pre-slicing fragments the ownership question into twelve near-identical cards and twelve triage passes, while the thing that actually needs to exist is **one declared population with one owner** (the discipline this seat wrote into #17797). ⇒ **A taker may land it per area file — each slice as a `Part of #<this card>` PR.** ⛔ What is not available is closing this card with rows still on the ledger.

## ⚠️ The constraint that makes each repair a judgement, not a rename

Floors have **almost no headroom**: `access-security`, `ai`, `approvals`, `attachments-storage`, `cli`, `dashboards`, `i18n`, `integration-system`, `search`, `studio-authoring` are **at** their floor. ⇒ ⛔ **Dropping a `#symbol` is not available.** Every row must be re-pointed, and the re-point needs a reading of what the prose actually means.

## Acceptance

1. Rows leave `SHARED_RESOLVER_RESIDUAL` **only by repair**, and the ceiling drops with them. ⛔ Never by raising the ceiling, ⛔ never by widening `symbol-anchors.mjs`, ⛔ never by lowering a file floor.
2. ⭐ **Per row, say which it was**: a genuinely wrong citation (re-pointed), or a correct citation the shared accept-set refuses (⇒ that row belongs to **#18101**, ⛔ not here).
3. ⭐ **Positive control per slice**: show the repaired anchor now resolves **through the shared resolver**, and that an unrelated row still reds. ⛔ A slice that only removes rows cannot show it repaired anything.
4. The `detector-artifact` row is one of the 47: this gate's own `SYMBOL_ANCHOR` detector truncates an item-id reference at its first hyphen and **manufactures a phantom anchor** (`…/access-security.json#access` from a citation reading `…json#access (access-security.scope-depth-asymmetry …)`). ⚠️ That is a **detector** defect, not a resolution one — repairing it means fixing the detector, not the citation.

## ⚠️ A maintainer-owned line this card cannot fix

`scripts/checklist-symbol-anchor-baseline.json`'s `$comment` now says something false: 「Each entry is the count of anchors that RESOLVED in that family file」 — an entry is now *resolved + residual*.

⛔ That file is **maintainer-only by its own `$authority` line**, and PR #18100 correctly did not touch it. The receiving dev's reasoning is the ruling and is worth repeating: reading the authority line narrowly — as scoping only to *lowering* a floor — **「is the move the line exists to stop.」** ⇒ ⛔ No dev on this card edits it either. It is a one-sentence maintainer edit, recorded here so it has a durable home rather than living in a session's memory.

## Links

- PR #18100 / card #16898 — the binding that created the residual, with the four-leg ablation proving the ledger exact in both directions.
- **#18101** — the 8 `accept-set` rows (the shared resolver refusing real declaration sites). ⛔ Different card, ⛔ different fix.

<sub>`domain:devx` execution PM seat · `session_012GKcPZbMoGq7WPzKLfRBTU` · seat post #6023 · row counts and floor readings are PR #18100's, cited as its; this seat verified the ledger mechanism (`SHARED_RESOLVER_RESIDUAL_CEILING = 55` at `:1623`, the D3 self-test at `:1825`) on that branch</sub>
